summary: Jefferson County fire tower on Holsclaw Hill, built 1947 (sources give 90, 100 or 200 ft); dismantled in 2004 per a 2009 culture-history report.

facts.status_note: Dismantled in 2004 per the 2009 culture-history report; no source describes what remains on the hill.

staffing.status: lookout man approved for appointment in October 1947; report says often staffed by Merle Ingram (undated)

access.note: Jefferson Memorial Forest has nearly 60 miles of hiking and equestrian trails. The lookout itself is gone.

events.note: Erected on Holsclaw Hill per the 2009 report; a late-October 1947 item said the tower would be completed the next day

Jefferson County Squirrel Club: climbers were inducted into the club (2009 report); a January 1948 story describes the membership test and gives the tower as 200 ft
Notice dated April 8, 1950 said a Louisville Astronomical Society star party would be held at the tower; public invited

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Accounts give 90 ft (April 1947 plan), 100 ft (December 1946 plan; the 2009 report's built height) and 200 ft (January 1948 club story). The record keeps 100 ft (30.5 m), the height the 2009 report gives for the tower as built.
Spelled Holsclaw in the Courier-Journal clippings and the 2009 report, and Holzclaw in the Forest Lookouts page title and the 1948 club story. The record keeps Holsclaw.

sources.title: Holzclaw - Forest Lookouts (Jefferson County clippings from the Courier-Journal and Freeport Journal-Standard)
The Culture History of the Jefferson Memorial Forest, final report (Cultural Resources Report TR8009, dated June 24, 2009)
sources.publisher: Corn Island Archaeology LLC for Louisville Metro Parks

notes_for_editor: The 1947 build date rests on the 2009 report and an October 1947 item saying completion was due the next day. The report's title page is dated June 24, 2009; an earlier draft wrongly gave 2008. The height is 100 ft in the 2009 report; 90 ft is an April 1947 plan and 200 ft a 1948 humorous club story. The view area conflicts (10,000 acres in the 1946 talk, nearly 35,000 in the 2009 report) and is left as stated in the story. The 2004 dismantling rests on one report, which cites a JMF 2008 source (the 2008 master plan) not checked here. No source describes the site today. Courier-Journal items were read only as transcribed on the Forest Lookouts page. The 1950 item is a notice of a planned star party, so the story says it was announced, not that it was held.
